idea: Prompt and workflow library product for equity analysts
buyer: Individual analysts and small research teams
pain: Analysts use AI badly because nobody has codified the good patterns
v1: A library of 60 tested analyst workflows
verdict: Great leverage, but the price is far too low to reach the target from her network.

why.distribution: Directly reachable analyst network, and a low price makes trial easy.
why.demand: Inferred from her adoption work; prompt libraries are widely given away free.
why.fmf: She codified exactly these patterns for a real firm - the content would be genuinely good.
why.revenue_structure: Low-priced monthly subscription with high churn risk.
why.defensibility: Prompt libraries are copied within days and models keep making them obsolete.
why.time_to_revenue: Building a credible library first: 3-6 months.
why.tailwind: AI adoption is strong, though prompt libraries specifically are being obsoleted by better models.
why.ceiling: £40/mo x 415 seats = £199k - an audience of hundreds she does not remotely have.

ceiling_arithmetic: £40/mo x 415 seats = £199k. Reaching 415 paying individual analysts requires an audience an order of magnitude beyond her network. Realistic: 40-60 seats = £19-29k.
carries: Genuine leverage and content she is unusually qualified to write.
kills: Price. At £40/month the volume needed is unreachable, and prompt libraries are the fastest-depreciating asset in AI.
test: Ask ten analysts whether they would pay £40/month for tested workflows.
test_pass: Most say yes and several ask when.
test_fail: They say they would expect it free, which is the likely answer.
